title: SF Chronicle: ICE Has Not Paid for Detainee Medical Care Since October 2025; Advocates Call It 'Death Policy'
excerpt: A San Francisco Chronicle investigation found that ICE stopped paying third-party outside medical providers in October 2025 after the VA ended a longstanding billing arrangement, leaving hospitals owed millions and causing delayed or canceled care for detainees with serious conditions including cancer and dialysis needs.
content:
The San Francisco Chronicle published an investigation revealing that ICE had not paid outside medical providers for detainee care since October 3, 2025, when the Department of Veterans Affairs abruptly ended a longstanding agreement to process ICE's medical claims from third-party specialists.

  • ICE's own internal contracting documents described the situation as an "absolute emergency" requiring immediate resolution "to prevent any further medical complications or loss of life."
  • The payment breakdown coincided with record detention numbers and a $104 billion ICE budget, and left hospitals and ambulance services owed millions, contributing to delayed or canceled specialty care including oncology, dialysis, and chemotherapy.
  • Some facilities billed detainees directly for care they are legally entitled to receive free, including a $634 blood test charge and a $17,210 hospital bill for emergency gallbladder surgery on a detainee handcuffed to his bed.
  • UC Berkeley law dean Erwin Chemerinsky said the billing practice was unconstitutional, as federal law requires the government to cover medical costs for people in its custody.
  • Advocacy groups labeled the situation a "death policy," with Adina Applebaum of the Amica Center for Immigrant Rights calling it "a deliberate policy choice, not an accident."

The Chronicle documented individual cases including Rodrigo, a 58-year-old green-card holder and cancer patient who was denied an oncologist appointment for months while ICE simultaneously tried to deport him, as medical staff requested outside oncology evaluation that ICE refused to authorize.
